why_this_refreeze_exists: the v1 manifest never covered mem0_breadth_arms.py or run_breadth_reader.py, because neither file existed yet at v1 freeze time. Both were then written and run in the same session without a refreeze. This is not a cap-wiring-only refreeze: while verifying it, a real bug was found in mem0_breadth_arms.py's truncate() (continue instead of break on overflow) and fixed. Recorded explicitly rather than glossed over.

unchanged_verified_by_hash: retrieval and ranking (mem0_adapter.py, mem0_probe.py, run_pilot.py all hash-identical to v1 and to clean-mem0.json's own recorded runner_digest/adapter_digest)
reader prompt and parameters (fixed_reader.py hash-identical to v1; run_breadth_reader.py imports READER_PROMPT/READER_PARAMS rather than restating them)
judge protocol templates, label rule and parameters (judge_pilot.py hash-identical to v1; run_breadth_judge.py imports them rather than restating them)
genuinely_new_since_v1: mem0_breadth_arms.py: new file at v1 freeze time, now exists. No provider calls. Builds arms from clean-mem0.json's persisted native + deep contexts.

run_breadth_reader.py: new file at v1 freeze time, now exists. Adds the corrected 3-way cap split (--cap-usd run ceiling, --total-cap-usd scope ceiling, --cap-scope) that v1's sibling fixed_reader.py never had.

run_breadth_judge.py: new file, added this session. Imports judge_pilot.py's protocol unchanged and adds the same 3-way cap split, because judge_pilot.py's own SpendLedger call has no total_cap_usd/cap_scope and was never going to be scope-tracked otherwise.

bug_found_and_fixed_this_session.defect: used `continue` instead of `break` when an item did not fit the token budget, so it skipped an oversized item and kept scanning for a smaller later one instead of stopping. Violates the frozen truncation rule (whole items, ranked order, STOP on first overflow, no skip-on-overflow).
bug_found_and_fixed_this_session.measured_impact: 17 of 30 (unit,budget) truncations at 500 and 1000 tokens produced a different kept-item set than the correct stop-on-overflow rule; 0 of 10 at 3000 tokens (every unit's full deep retrieval already fits under 3000, so no truncation ever triggers there). gold_in_context/gold_rank labels were unaffected for all 40 arms (0 changed) -- the bug changed which filler items surrounded the gold, not whether gold was retrieved.
bug_found_and_fixed_this_session.same_latent_pattern_elsewhere_NOT_fixed_: scripts/arena/mechanism_ablation.py has byte-identical truncate() logic (also `continue`), which is what produced the reused Hindsight 4/6/6/7 curve. Not touched: Hindsight is out of scope for this experiment per explicit instruction not to rerun it. Flagged as an open question for a separate decision, not investigated further here.
bug_found_and_fixed_this_session.fix: changed continue to break; added tests/test_mem0_breadth_arms.py (5 tests) pinning the stop-on-overflow, prefix-only, whole-items-only behavior.
bug_found_and_fixed_this_session.remediation: arms rebuilt (free, no provider calls); only the 17 affected (arm,question_id) reader calls were re-run against corrected context (run_breadth_reader.py --arms mem0-breadth-arms-delta.json), not all 40; the 23 unaffected original answers were kept and merged in unchanged. The original flawed arms/outputs are retained on disk as *-SUPERSEDED-skip-on-overflow-bug.* for audit, not deleted.

truncation_rule: whole evidence items, original ranked order, add while the next fits; STOP (break) on first overflow; no skip-on-overflow; no re-ranking; no gold-aware selection
token_budget_rules: identical to v1; unaffected by the bugfix, which changed which items are kept under an unchanged budget ceiling, not the ceiling itself
ranking_context_assembly_rules: native = Mem0 limit=10 result verbatim; wider arms = prefix of one deeper limit=400 call on the same ranking, truncated by the (now-corrected) whole-item budget rule. Both calls read one clean ingest; no re-retrieval.
superseded_artifacts_stay_invalid: every prior Mem0 artefact still keeps INVALIDATED_BY_CROSS_UNIT_CONTAMINATION; this refreeze does not restore any old Mem0 conclusion
